Leave Across the Six GCC Countries Compared

Enter your monthly wage and the number of sick days to see the comparison across the six countries, then the annual and sick leave tables.

Prepared and reviewed by the Mustahaqati team · Last updated: 2026-11-03

How much are you paid for sick days in each country?

In local currency; we assume the same wage in every country.

Frequently asked questions

Which Gulf country gives the longest annual leave?

The UAE, Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain give 30 days a year (in Kuwait, 30 working days excluding rest days and holidays). Saudi Arabia gives 21 days, rising to 30 after 5 years, and Qatar 21 days, rising to 28 after 5 years.

Which country gives the longest paid sick leave?

Oman: up to 182 days a year with pay falling in steps from full to 35%. Saudi Arabia follows with 90 paid days (30 full and 60 at three-quarters), then Kuwait and the UAE.

Is sick leave paid during probation?

In the UAE there is no paid sick leave during probation. In Qatar and Bahrain three months of service are required. The details are on each country's page.

Which wage is sick pay based on?

It varies: Qatar uses basic salary; Kuwait, Oman and Bahrain the full wage; Saudi Arabia the actual wage (basic plus fixed allowances); and the UAE the full wage by the wording of the law, though practice differs. The comparison uses one wage for simplicity, so use your country's calculator for an exact figure.

Sources

  • UAE — Federal Decree-Law 33/2021, Articles 29 and 31 (MOHRE)
  • Saudi Arabia — Labour Law, Articles 109 and 117 (HRDF, English)
  • Oman — Labour Law RD 53/2023, Articles 78–82 (Arabic)
  • Bahrain — Labour Law 36/2012, official English translation (LMRA)
  • Kuwait — Law 6/2010, Articles 69 and 70 (Arabic)
